Sam: Quick heads-up — ran nightly perf suite with FP8/CUTLASS toggles enabled on a prod-like node. Seeing ~12-18% throughput drop for 4-bit kernels when KV cache hit rate >60%. Posting quick traces.

bench-bot: [auto-bench 1712056789]
Throughput tokens/s: baseline=18900, fp8-kernels=16500 (-12.7%)
P95 latency(ms): baseline=86, fp8=104 (+21%)
Config: GPU=A100-40GB, CUDA=12.2, Triton=2.11, CUTLASS=3.2

Maya: Did you repro locally or only on the nightly cluster?

Sam: Repro'd on dev01 with the same container image. Memory use slightly lower (~-6%) but observed a hot path: extra pack/unpack for KV cache when using the quantized attention kernel.

Anya: That sounds like a calibration / packing mismatch. We switch to dynamic per-tensor scale today; per-channel would avoid unpack on cache hits. Can you paste perf top?

Sam: Perf top snapshot (truncated):
```
  28.4%  attention_forward_quantize
  22.1%  cutlass_gemm_int4_launcher
  15.7%  kv_cache_pack_unaligned
  9.3%   memcpy_h2d
  7.8%   triton_fused_attention
```

Sam: Also repro: forcing INT8 path via build flag (-DUSE_INT8_KERNEL=ON) recovered throughput to ~18.7k but degraded answer quality slightly on one eval set.

Oliver: Can you confirm REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY? runtime chooses kernel families by that. If set to "auto" it picks CUTLASS for many dims which might introduce extra packing.

Sam: It was set to "auto" for the run. I flipped to "latency" and got throughput back to ~19100 tokens/s, but p95 became more variable on short sequences.

Liam: FYI we've seen device-query quirks on the custom AMI where sm capability was reported as sm_80 even for patched H100 images — can cause CUTLASS to pick incorrect codegen. Did you run deviceQuery?

Sam: DeviceQuery output:
```
  Name: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
  CUDA Driver: 535.86
  CUDA Runtime: 12.2
  SM: 8.0
```
No obvious mismatch.

Maya: Two things to investigate: (1) runtime sanity check to only pick CUTLASS FP8 kernels when compute capability >= sm_80 AND compiled-with-sm80 flag present, (2) improve quant calibration to per-channel for Q/K/V to avoid unpacking on KV cache hits.

Anya: Agreed. Implementation note: if we store per-head scales in kv_meta we can skip a per-request dequantize when there's a cache hit. That should amortize calibration overhead. Prototype idea:
```diff
- quantize_qkv(tensor)
+ quantize_qkv_per_channel(tensor, scales)
  // compute scales per head, store in kv_meta
```

Oliver: Also consider exposing runtime kernel override via console and an env var REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL_FAMILY={triton,cutlass,int8}. Useful for quick rollbacks.

Sam: Quick repro patch I tried: set REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=latency and REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL_FAMILY=triton on prod-sim node => throughput stable and p95 improved for short seqs. Will run full bench matrix.

Liam: We should also add a compile-time guard: cmake flags we used may disable fallback. Example build snippet we test with:
```
cmake .. -DUSE_CUTLASS_FP8=ON -DUSE_INT8_KERNEL=OFF -DCUDA_ARCHS="80;90" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
make -j48
```
If arch list mismatches device the runtime may pick a slower generic kernel.

Maya: Action items: Sam prototype per-channel calibrator + KV metadata (3d), Anya add runtime kernel-policy override & console toggle (2d), Oliver add deviceQuery + build-flag sanity log (1d), Liam run bench matrix across A100/H100/RTX6000 (4d).

Anya: Small note — calibration quality vs speed tradeoff: per-channel improves perf but costs a bit in calibration time/complexity. We'll add a fallback to per-tensor for tiny models.

Sam: I'll attach microbench numbers to this thread when available. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

Maya: If Sam posts the microbench, I'll add a perf test in eng-releases CI to catch regressions earlier. :mag:

Oliver: +1. Also let's add a small end-to-end eval run so we track quality delta when we toggle INT8/FP8 kernels.

Sam: Will do. Follow-up soon.
